newsitem.title: UK: UK building skill shortage inflates tender prices.
newsitem.headline: UK building skill shortage inflates tender prices.

text.p: Britain's Construction Confederation said on Tuesday a skills shortage in the industry had already started to push up wages and was leading to higher tender prices for projects.

As the industry enters its fifth consecutive quarter of growth after five years of recession, building firms are "having difficulty in securing labour, especially bricklayers," said Martin Laing, president of the Confederation.
"It is obviously having an impact. That's why tender prices are rising," he told reporters.
But the shortage of labour extends to other areas of the workforce.

Construction Industry Council (CIC) chief executive Graham Watts, told Reuters construction firms were also having problems employing skilled people like architects and engineers which the CIC represents.
The industry axed more than 500,000 jobs during its 1990-95 recession. Laing admitted it was an industry challenge to tempt these people back and persuade them to stay for the long term.
The construction industry is seeking to address the skills crisis by trying to get government funding for training under its welfare-to-work programme.

"We have been talking to the government about Welfare to Work," said Ian Deslandes, chief executive of the Construction Confederation add that the initial government reaction to their proposals was "very good".
The two sides hope to have pilot scheme up and running within six months.

The Confederation denied it faced a potential squeeze on capacity with a number of major construction projects due to come on stream, including the Channel Tunnel Rail Link and the second terminal at Manchester airport.
"The industry sees growth at 4-5 percent ahead and that is manageable," said Laing.
